content: Our Lady of Fatima University, previously known as Our Lady of Fatima College, is a private educational institution located in the Philippines. It operates two primary campuses, one situated in Valenzuela City and the other in Quezon City. The university primarily focuses on allied medical sciences. Its name is derived from the Philippine National Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima, also known as Pambansang Dambana ng Birhen ng Fatima in Tagalog, which is located near the Valenzuela campus. However, the university is not affiliated with the Catholic Church and accepts students from all religious backgrounds. The university was established in Valenzuela in 1967 by Jose C. Olivares and his son-in-law, Dr. Vicente M. Santos. It originated from the Our Lady of Fatima Hospital, which served as the main provider of medical and healthcare services in Valenzuela. Jose Olivares was an entrepreneur and a former chemistry professor at Ateneo de Manila University and the University of the Philippines. Dr. Santos, who came from humble beginnings in Hagonoy, Bulacan, graduated from the University of Santo Tomas, became an obstetrician-gynecologist, and delivered over 96,000 babies during his 40-year career. The institution upholds the virtues of veritas et misericordia, which translates to truth and compassion in Latin. The founders aimed to transform the hospital from a general healthcare facility into a teaching hospital for healthcare professionals, including nurses and midwives. This vision materialized in 1973 with the establishment of the Our Lady of Fatima College of Nursing. The first graduating class in 1976 achieved a remarkable 100% passing rate in the Nursing Board Examinations. Dr. Santos and his wife, Juliet Olivares-Santos, continued to expand the institution, founding the Fatima College of Medicine in 1979. While the university remains focused on medical education, it diversified its programs in the 1990s, introducing courses in computer science, maritime education, and business. The institution achieved university status in December 2002, with Dr. Vicente Santos serving as its founding president. After his passing, his wife assumed the role of president. The university's programs in Nursing, Physical Therapy, and Dental Medicine are accredited by the Philippine Association of Colleges and Universities Commission on Accreditation (PACUCOA). Additionally, its graduate school has been accredited by the Association of Schools, Colleges, and Universities AAI. The Fatima College of Medicine holds accreditation from the New York State Education Department and the Illinois State Board of Education. The College of Maritime Education is ISO 9001:2000 certified and is listed on the Commission on Higher Education's (CHED) white list as a qualified provider of maritime education. CHED recognized the university's significant contributions to tertiary education in the Philippines and the Asia-Pacific region, as well as its commitment to quality education, research, and community service, granting it regulation status through CHED Resolution No. 393-2003 on October 27, 2003. On August 26, 2007, Darlene Chutuap, a student from Fatima, achieved the highest score (88%) in the 2007 Nursing Licensure Examinations (NLE), which had 64,908 examinees, as reported by the Professional Regulations Commission. Fatima also excelled in the Physician Licensure Examination conducted by the Board of Medicine on August 15, 2007, with its graduate, Ma. Fatima, achieving a top score of 92% among 2,656 examinees.
